transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

I'm here because lately I just can't keep my head clear at work. It's becoming a real problem. I'm a therapist, and I find myself losing track of what my clients are saying right in the middle of a session. I end up rereading the same chart note over and over because it just doesn't sink in. And then I just freeze on simple decisions that I used to handle without even thinking.
When did you first notice these difficulties?

It's been... well, about a month now. It started right around the time the clinic lost some staff. My schedule ended up shifting into late-evening coverage, and I've had to handle a lot heavier crisis paperwork. So, yeah, right around then is when I first noticed it.
How has your sleep been since these concentration problems began?

It hasn't been great, honestly. I'll get home from the clinic just... completely exhausted. But then I get in bed and I just lie there for hours. My mind just keeps replaying the day, over and over. And then, if I actually do manage to fall asleep, I end up waking up way before my alarm even goes off. I just wake up feeling like I barely slept at all.
Since these problems began, have you been feeling persistently down or hopeless?

Not really, no. I mean, I'm frustrated, for sure, because I can't seem to do my job right lately. But... I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless about everything. It's mostly just that I'm aggravated by the brain fog and not being able to sleep.
Since these problems began, have you been experiencing excessive worry that feels difficult to control?

No, not really. I mean, I stress about getting my paperwork done, sure, but... it's not like an out-of-control worry. It's just the normal amount of stress you'd expect from falling behind at work. I don't feel like my mind is constantly racing with worries about everything else, if that makes sense.
Before this past month, did you regularly have similar problems with concentration?

No, not really. I mean, I've always been pretty good at focusing on my work. It's really just been this past month or so that things have gotten so bad. Before that, I didn't have any trouble getting my notes done or paying attention in sessions.
On days when you feel you have slept well, do you still have the same difficulty concentrating?

I'm not really sure. To be honest, I haven't actually had a night where I felt like I slept well since this all started a month ago. So... I can't really say if a good night's sleep would fix the concentration issues. I just haven't had one to compare it to.
When you try to sleep, do you have enough time and a suitable environment for sleep but still cannot fall or stay asleep?

Yeah, I have the time, and my bedroom is perfectly fine for sleeping. It's just... I get home tired, but then I end up lying there for hours just replaying the day in my head. And if I actually do manage to fall asleep, I always wake up way before my alarm, just feeling like I barely slept at all.
Do you have the same trouble sleeping on nights when you do not have work the next day?

I haven't really noticed a difference, to be honest. Um... even when I don't have to work the next day, it's pretty much the same. I just... I still can't seem to sleep. So, yeah, having a day off doesn't really seem to change anything.
Apart from the sleep and concentration problems, have you noticed any other significant emotional or behavioral changes since the clinic staffing changes?

No, not really. I mean... I guess I just feel tired and out of it all the time because of the sleep thing, but... no, I haven't noticed any other big changes like that. It's mostly just the sleep and not being able to focus.
Do you sleep better when you are away from your usual bedroom, such as when staying at a hotel or on vacation?

I haven't really stayed anywhere else lately, so I don't know for sure. Um... I haven't been on a vacation or stayed in a hotel in a while. So, yeah, I'm not really sure if being away from my own bedroom would make a difference or not.
When you are lying awake at night, are your thoughts mainly focused on work and the clinic staffing changes?

Not really. I mean... sometimes work crosses my mind, but it's not like I'm just lying there dwelling on the clinic changes. My mind just kind of... wanders, I guess. Mostly I just stare at the ceiling feeling frustrated that I'm still awake. So, no, it's not really focused on one specific thing like that.
How many nights per week do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

It's pretty much every night. I get home from work just completely tired, but then I get into bed and... I just lie there for hours. It's like my brain just keeps replaying the whole day over and over. And even if I finally do manage to fall asleep, I always end up waking up way before my alarm goes off. When I get up, I feel like I barely slept at all.
When you lie awake in bed, do you feel tense or keyed up even when you are not thinking about anything specific?

Not really. I don't think I feel... tense, exactly. Like, my body isn't on edge or anything like that. I'm usually just lying there feeling completely exhausted. So, no, I wouldn't say I feel keyed up, just mostly annoyed that I'm still awake and can't drift off.
Apart from the sleep and concentration difficulties, how distressed do you feel about the clinic staffing changes themselves?

Honestly, I'm not really distressed about them at all. I mean... it's just work. People come and go at the clinic, so it's not something that bothers me on a personal level. I just go in and do my job. So, no, the changes themselves aren't really upsetting me or anything like that.
